summary_short: The total conscious time spent by every human who has ever lived, estimated with a Fermi-style population integral.
description_medium: The total conscious time spent by every human who has ever lived is large enough to feel geological, yet still tiny beside the biosphere that carried humans the whole time. It is a useful reminder that human history is only one thin slice of the planet's much longer clock.

summary_short: Mammals occupy a surprisingly modest slice of deep time compared with insects or microbes.
description_medium: Mammals occupy a surprisingly modest slice of deep time compared with insects or microbes, but their total accumulated life still jumps far beyond the human story. This is where a clade-wide total starts to feel ecological rather than historical.

summary_short: Vertebrates are the animal branch people notice first, but most of their total lifetime is not in the big land animals.
description_medium: Vertebrates are the animal branch people notice first, but most of their total lifetime is not in the big land animals. Fish and other small, numerous species quietly dominate the count, which is why this total is much larger than intuition suggests.

summary_short: Insects are where the tally starts to feel almost absurd.
description_medium: Insects are where the tally starts to feel almost absurd. Their bodies are small and their generations are short, so abundance and turnover do most of the work once you start adding up everything that has ever lived.

summary_short: Once you sum every animal hour ever lived, individual species stop mattering much.
description_medium: Once you sum every animal hour ever lived, individual species stop mattering much and turnover takes over. The result feels less like a list of creatures and more like a statistical property of the living world.

summary_short: Plants stretch time differently from animals because they are long-lived, widespread, and often present as standing biomass for years at a stretch.
description_medium: Plants stretch time differently from animals because they are long-lived, widespread, and often present as standing biomass for years at a stretch. Their accumulated hours pile up across seasons, forests, and whole landscapes rather than across brief lifetimes.

summary_short: Fungi are easy to overlook because much of them is hidden underground or inside wood.
description_medium: Fungi are easy to overlook because much of them is hidden underground or inside wood. That hidden network makes them a good reminder that biological scale is not always what meets the eye.

summary_short: Microbes dominate life by both count and turnover.
description_medium: Microbes dominate life by both count and turnover, so even tiny lifetimes accumulate into something immense. This is the point where the biosphere stops feeling like a collection of organisms and starts feeling like a planetary process.

summary_short: The sum of every organism-hour ever lived on Earth.
description_medium: This is the sum of every organism-hour ever lived on Earth. Almost all of it is microbes, which is why the number shoots past every animal and plant benchmark on the way to the full history of life.
